question:
A point charge $q = 4 \times 10^{-9}\text{ C}$ is fixed in air. A test charge $q_0 = 2 \times 10^{-6}\text{ C}$ is moved slowly from a point $A$ at $0.20\text{ m}$ from $q$ to a point $B$ at $0.50\text{ m}$ from $q$.
Find
(i) the potentials at $A$ and $B$, and
(ii) the work done by the electrostatic field in this displacement. Take $\frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0} = 9 \times 10^9\text{ N m}^2\text{ C}^{-2}$.

options.A:
(i) $V_A=72\,\text{V}$ and $V_B=180\,\text{V}$
(ii) Work done by electrostatic field $=-2.16\times10^{-4}\,\text{J}$
options.B:
(i) $V_A=180\,\text{V}$ and $V_B=72\,\text{V}$
(ii) Work done by electrostatic field $=q_0(V_A-V_B)=2.16\times10^{-4}\,\text{J}$
options.C:
(i) $V_A=180\,\text{V}$ and $V_B=72\,\text{V}$
(ii) Work done by electrostatic field $=0$
options.D:
(i) $V_A=90\,\text{V}$ and $V_B=36\,\text{V}$
(ii) Work done by electrostatic field $=1.08\times10^{-4}\,\text{J}$
